note: Robinson, TX -- the 'Height and Area Regulations' table for each of the 14 Euclidean base districts, read from Article 6 (ZONING DISTRICTS) of the City of Robinson Zoning Ordinance. ROUTE: the ordinance text was read as rendered HTML on Zoneomics (citation_url; the site splits the ordinance one article per page, and .../robinson-TX/chapter_6 is Article 6), which reproduces each district's Height and Area Regulations table cell-for-cell including the ord.-number currency line under each table. Robinson's own official code is published on Municode at library.municode.com/tx/robinson/codes/code_of_ordinances; a plain fetch of the Municode ordinance pages returns a JavaScript shell with no server-rendered ordinance text, so Municode could NOT be read this pass and is NOT the source of any value in this table. The Zoneomics route is therefore a hard-to-reproduce-without-a-browser route in the sense that the reading step was a rendered page, but it is a live, fetchable, stable URL -- not a dead mirror. CROSS-CHECK: the same district tables appear with the same figures in City of Robinson agenda packets published on the city's own site -- 2020-06-30 (SF-3), 2020-12-22 (SF-2), 2023-06-22 (SF-1 plus an AG/RE comparison table) -- each at robinsontexas.org/AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Agenda/... Those are independently fetchable and independently reproduce the SF-1, SF-2 and SF-3 rows coded here; the remaining 11 rows rest on the Article 6 read alone. VINTAGE: every table carries 'Ord. No. 2022-019, Sec. 1(Exh. A), 7-5-22' as its adoption line, and the ten districts that Ord. 2024-023 touched (AG, RE, SF-1, SF-2, SF-3, 2F, PH, MF-1, MF-2, MH) carry 'Ord. No. 2024-023, Sec. N, 9-3-24' as their currency line. So the dimensional standards coded here are current through Ordinance 2024-023, adopted 2024-09-03, read at source (not inferred). R/O, C-1, C-2 and I carry the 2022-019 line only. OMITTED: PDD (Planned Development District, Section 3.4) -- Section 3.4.4 says the development requirements for each PDD 'shall be set forth in the amending ordinance granting that PDD district', so PDD has no district table and is a per-ordinance shape rather than a missing standard (recorded as out-of-scope-pud in the lane fragment). NON-SCALAR / CONDITIONAL VALUES FLAGGED not_specified: (1) AG and RE state building coverage as '50% for rear half of lot', which is not a percent-of-lot-area figure -- coded 50 with not_specified true and the cell quoted verbatim. (2) PH's side yard is an asymmetric alternative ('5 ft. minimum; or one side 8 in. minimum / other side 10 ft. minimum') -- coded 5 with not_specified true. (3) PH's front yard is two different numbers by element ('20 ft. garage; 15 ft. living area minimum') -- coded 15 (the living-area figure) with not_specified true. (4) AG/RE, R/O, C-1, C-2 and I state no impervious-coverage figure at all -- coded 100 with not_specified true. (5) R/O, C-1, C-2 and I state height as a front-setback-line figure with a trade-up ('40 ft at front setback line ... one additional foot of height per foot of additional setback, not to exceed 60 ft'), so max_height_ft is coded at the binding base and the trade-up is preserved verbatim in the quote at reduced confidence; I's 45/90/170 ft graduated envelope is handled the same way. Single-side vs combined-side: SF-1 and SF-2 state a single-side minimum plus a combined-both-sides minimum ('10 ft. min. one side & 15 ft. min. total both sides'). The single-side figure is coded as side_ft and the full clause is quoted, per the same convention as belton-tx.json's conditional-exception handling. P-299 OT-2 (2026-09-17): this table's 98 primary-source-verified value slots are RELABELLED to "transcription-read", the fourth verification state added to gate.ts in the same change, with confidence capped at 0.75 (rule G9). Reason, from this file's own note above: every value here was read through a COPY of the governing instrument rather than off the instrument's own text -- rendered HTML on Zoneomics, a live third-party mirror of the city's ordinance. The state is not a downgrade of the read's quality; it is the honest name for the channel, and it keeps "primary-source-verified" meaning what it says for the tables that did reach the instrument's own text. It is treated exactly like primary-source-verified for rule G2 (no code-section atom is required) and skips G5's quote round-trip for the same reason.

max_height_ft.quote: Section 6.17.4 (Maximum building height): Forty-five feet of building height is permitted within the first 100 feet from the property line of nearest residential uses; and may increase one additional foot of height for each additional foot of setback to a height of 90 feet; except that one-third of a building's footprint may be up to 170 feet in height when located at least 300 feet from the property line of nearest residential uses. This is a graduated envelope, not a flat maximum; 45 ft (the near-residential base) is coded.
